title: Virginia Halloween Alert: Richmond-Norfolk Safety Tips for Oct. 31 - NewsBreak
text:
By Cole Barrett ,
1 days ago
Photo: Country Herald
Richmond, VA – Halloween is just days away, and families from Richmond to Virginia Beach and communities across Virginia are preparing for a Saturday evening filled with costumes, candy and trick-or-treating. With fading daylight, busy intersections and children walking through residential neighborhoods, parents should take important precautions before heading out Oct. 31.
According to the National Safety Council, pedestrian visibility, traffic awareness and adult supervision are important precautions for reducing Halloween-related injuries.
Here are 10 essential safety steps Virginia families should follow, from getting ready at home to returning safely with Halloween candy.
Before Heading Out 1. Plan Your Trick-or-Treating Route
Choose familiar, well-lit neighborhoods and check local trick-or-treating hours. Establish a return time and meeting location, especially for older children heading out in groups.
2. Choose Safe, Comfortable Costumes
Avoid oversized shoes, dragging fabric and masks that restrict vision. Comfortable footwear is important on sidewalks, neighborhood steps and uneven driveways.
3. Make Costumes Visible to Drivers
Add reflective tape to costumes and candy bags. Carry flashlights or glow sticks to help motorists spot children after sunset.
4. Prepare for Virginia's Fall Weather
Late October can bring chilly evenings, coastal winds and rain, with cooler conditions possible in western Virginia. Check Saturday's local forecast and dress children in comfortable layers appropriate for the weather.
While Trick-or-Treating 5. Stay Together and Stay Alert
Young children should remain with a responsible adult. Older children should travel in groups, carry charged phones and check in regularly.
6. Walk, Don't Run
Use sidewalks whenever available. Where sidewalks are missing, walk facing traffic and remain as far from moving vehicles as safely possible.
7. Watch for Cars at Every Crossing
Cross at intersections, obey traffic signals and look both ways. Never assume approaching vehicles will stop. Drivers should slow down in residential neighborhoods.
8. Be Careful at Every Door
Approach well-lit homes, remain outside when collecting candy and never enter unfamiliar homes, apartment buildings or vehicles.
After Returning Home 9. Inspect Halloween Candy
Parents should examine treats for damaged packaging, potential allergens and choking hazards. Discard anything questionable before children begin eating.
10. Keep Halloween Decorations Fire-Safe
Use battery-operated LED candles instead of open flames inside jack-o'-lanterns. Keep costumes and decorations away from heaters and other heat sources.
A Final Reminder for Virginia Families With Halloween falling on Saturday, Oct. 31, families should prepare for increased pedestrian activity throughout the evening.
From Richmond and Virginia Beach to Norfolk, Chesapeake, Newport News, Roanoke, Alexandria and Arlington, motorists should remain especially alert after sunset.
Parents in urban neighborhoods should watch for turning vehicles at busy intersections, while families in suburban and rural communities should take extra precautions on poorly lit roads.
A few simple precautions can help ensure Halloween ends with candy, costumes and happy memories instead of preventable emergencies.
